title: Split Array With Minimum Difference
summary: Given an integer array nums, split it into two subarrays, left and right, such that left is strictly increasing and right is strictly decreasing.
statement: Given an integer array nums, split it into two subarrays, left and right, such that left is strictly increasing and right is strictly decreasing. Return the minimum possible absolute difference between the sums of left and right. If no valid split can be made, return -1.
constraints: nums has two to 100,000 positive integers.
Both nonempty parts must preserve the original contiguous order.
The left part is strictly increasing and the right part strictly decreasing; return negative one if no split qualifies.
hints: A cut is valid exactly when its entire prefix increases and its entire suffix decreases.
Precompute those two Boolean properties and scan all cuts while maintaining the left sum.
At every valid cut, compare the two sums and minimize their absolute difference.
The prefix and suffix flags certify every required adjacent comparison, and every possible nonempty split is inspected.
editorial: The prefix and suffix flags certify every required adjacent comparison, and every possible nonempty split is inspected.

tests.explanation: Splitting after three gives sums four and two, so the minimum difference is two.
The two valid cuts both have absolute difference four.
